page: Amazon Web Services m8g.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 2 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography but no hyperthreading. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a mix of average and weak performance profiles. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable strength, registering in the top 25% of benchmarks. However, multi-core and multi-threaded operations, such as stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, are weak. Memory bandwidth is average for large uncached blocks but weak for small cached blocks and large write blocks. Passmark CPU, extended instructions, and encryption tests score in the poor category, while database operations maintain an average rating.

The m8g.large offers a balanced resource profile for general-purpose workloads, presenting a cost-efficient entry point for ARM-based deployments that do not require high-density memory or local storage. Tradeoffs include limited multi-threaded scaling and poor performance in cryptographic and extended instruction sets. The instance is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic database operations, single-threaded file processing, and low-throughput static web serving.

It is best suited for lightweight database operations, single-threaded file processing, and low-traffic web serving.
